body:
A few use cases, a note on encoding, and a live repro — including a real-world infra gotcha.

**Why QUERY is a particularly good fit for forms**

Because QUERY is **safe and idempotent**, a `<form method="query">` submission would — unlike POST — be safely bookmarkable, re-runnable on back/forward navigation, and cacheable, while still carrying a request body. That fills a real gap, where complex read requests are forced into one of two imperfect options:

- **GET** with a long query string → URL length limits, awkward for nested/structured criteria.
- **POST** used for a read → semantically wrong; breaks caching, the back button, and link sharing.

Concrete use cases: faceted/advanced search, report builders, map bounding-box queries, and structured-query endpoints (e.g. GraphQL) driven by a plain HTML form with no JavaScript.

**On the open encoding question**

The natural default would be to reuse existing form serialization — `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` (and `multipart/form-data` via `enctype`) — placed in the request *body* instead of the URL. That keeps the authoring model identical to today's forms; the only change is *where* the bytes go. Worth deciding whether/how `Accept-Query` (RFC 10008) interacts with this.

**Relationship to #3577 / #11347 (PUT/PATCH/DELETE in forms)**

I'd argue QUERY should be considered separately and is the *easier* case. PUT/PATCH/DELETE are unsafe and raise real CORS/security questions for form submission. QUERY is safe + idempotent, so it sidesteps most of those — it's much closer to GET, just with a body. A lower-risk first step.

**Live repro of current behavior**

**Demo (no install):** https://samuel-ifrs.github.io/query-form-repro/
**Source + Node version:** https://github.com/samuel-ifrs/query-form-repro

- The `method="query"` form reaches the server as **GET** — the body is silently dropped, because an unknown form method falls back to GET. (The `get`/`post` controls behave as expected.)
- `fetch(url, { method: 'QUERY', body })` *does* send QUERY on the wire (the Node server logs `actual=QUERY` same-origin), so the method is already reachable from script — just not from declarative forms.

**One infra data point worth flagging for rollout**

While building the repro I tried hosting the echo endpoint behind LiteSpeed (a very common web server): it rejects QUERY at the request parser with `400 "It is not a valid request!"` — before the app runs, and not fixable via `.htaccess`/WAF config. So even where the browser side lands, end-to-end QUERY will depend on server/WAF stacks recognizing the method. Not a blocker for this issue, but relevant to how broadly `<form method="query">` would actually work in the wild today.

Happy to help flesh out a spec PR for the form-submission side if there's implementer interest.
